title: Maravi empire founded
description: A paramount chief of the Phiri clan founds the Maravi confederacy around the lake, the state from which the country takes its name.

title: Bocarro crosses the country
description: The Portuguese trader Gaspar Bocarro journeys between Tete and Kilwa through what is now Malawi and leaves the first European account of it.

title: Livingstone reaches Lake Malawi
description: Acting on a tip from a Portuguese source, David Livingstone reaches the great lake which he names Lake Nyasa.

title: Scottish mission at Cape Maclear
description: Missionaries of the Free Church of Scotland establish the Livingstonia mission at the southern end of the lake.

title: African Lakes Company
description: Glasgow traders found the African Lakes Company to supply the missions, the seed of British commercial and political interest.

title: British Central Africa Protectorate
description: Facing Portuguese claims, Britain sets up a protectorate over the region; it becomes the Nyasaland Protectorate in 1907.

title: Chilembwe uprising
description: The Baptist pastor John Chilembwe leads an armed revolt against colonial rule and the First World War draft; it is crushed and he is killed within days.

title: Nyasaland African Congress
description: The country's first nationalist organisation is formed on the model of South Africa's ANC.

title: Banda returns
description: Hastings Banda comes home after forty-two years abroad to lead the campaign against the federation.

title: State of emergency
description: The colonial government declares an emergency, arrests Banda and hundreds of Congress supporters and flies in Rhodesian troops.

title: MCP sweeps elections
description: Banda's Malawi Congress Party wins an overwhelming victory in the Legislative Council elections.

title: Banda prime minister
description: With self-government following the death of the federation, Banda formally becomes prime minister of Nyasaland.

title: Independence
description: Exactly six years after Banda's return, Nyasaland becomes the independent Commonwealth realm of Malawi.

title: Cabinet Crisis
description: Banda sacks his whole cabinet after weeks of confrontation; the ex-ministers flee into exile and the way is open to one-man rule.

title: One-party republic
description: A new constitution makes Malawi a republic and a one-party state with Hastings Banda as president.

title: President for life
description: Parliament declares Banda president for life of Malawi, a year after his party gave him the same title within it.

title: Mwanza murders
description: Three ministers and an MP die in an official "traffic accident" later exposed as a regime murder.

title: Bishops' pastoral letter
description: The Catholic bishops' Lenten letter, read in every church, breaks the public silence against Banda's regime.

title: Multiparty referendum
description: Malawians vote in a referendum to end the one-party state in favour of multi-party democracy.

title: First free elections
description: Bakili Muluzi and his United Democratic Front beat Banda in the first free elections, ending thirty years of Banda's rule.

title: First democratic transition
description: Malawi sees its first transfer of power between democratically elected presidents as Bingu wa Mutharika wins.

title: Joyce Banda takes over
description: After Bingu wa Mutharika dies of a heart attack, Vice-President Joyce Banda becomes southern Africa's first female president.

title: Peter Mutharika wins
description: The late president's brother beats Joyce Banda, who finishes third, in a disputed but accepted election.

title: Disputed re-election
description: Peter Mutharika wins a narrow second term in a result soon overturned by the courts for fraud.
